claim: Morphogen profiles allow cells to determine their position within a developing organism.
source: Morphogen profiles allow cells to determine their position within a developing organism, but not all morphogen profiles form by the same mechanism.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about morphogen function in developmental biology.

claim: Not all morphogen profiles form by the same mechanism.
source: Morphogen profiles allow cells to determine their position within a developing organism, but not all morphogen profiles form by the same mechanism.
evidence: This is supported by references to different mechanisms (diffusion and direct transport) discussed throughout the manuscript and cited literature.

claim: Direct transport establishes a morphogen profile without adding noise in the process.
source: We find that direct transport establishes a morphogen profile without adding noise in the process.
evidence: This is a primary finding derived from the theoretical analysis presented in the manuscript, specifically the proof that DT follows birth-death statistics.

claim: For sufficiently large values of profile length, the diffusion mechanism is many times more precise than direct transport due to a higher refresh rate of morphogen molecules.
source: Despite this advantage, we find that for sufficiently large values of profile length, the diffusion mechanism is many times more precise due to a higher refresh rate of morphogen molecules.
evidence: This is a primary finding derived from theoretical calculations comparing the two models, shown in Figure 3B.

claim: There exists a profile lengthscale below which direct transport is more precise, and above which diffusion is more precise.
source: We predict a profile lengthscale below which direct transport is more precise, and above which diffusion is more precise.
evidence: This prediction is derived from theoretical analysis and shown in Figure 3B as a crossover point.

claim: The prediction of a crossover lengthscale is supported by data from a wide variety of morphogens in developing Drosophila and zebrafish.
source: This prediction is supported by data from a wide variety of morphogens in developing Drosophila and zebrafish.
evidence: This is supported by the comparison of theoretical predictions with experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Cells use positional information from morphogen profiles to determine their position with extremely high precision.
source: Cells use this information to determine their position with extremely high precision (Dubuis et al., 2013; Erdmann et al., 2009; Gregor et al., 2007a; Houchmandzadeh et al., 2002; de Lachapelle and Bergmann, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to experimental studies.

claim: In the synthesis-diffusion-clearance (SDC) model, morphogen molecules are produced by localized source cells and diffuse through extracellular space before degrading or being internalized by target cells.
source: One well-known mechanism is the synthesis-diffusion-clearance (SDC) model in which morphogen molecules are produced by localized source cells and diffuse through extracellular space before degrading or being internalized by target cells (Akiyama and Gibson, 2015; Gierer and Meinhardt, 1972; Lander et al., 2002; Müller et al., 2013; Rogers and Schier, 2011; Wilcockson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a description of the SDC model supported by multiple citations.

claim: In the direct transport (DT) model, morphogen molecules travel through protrusions called cytonemes directly from the source cells to the target cells.
source: Alternatively, a direct transport (DT) model has been proposed where morphogen molecules travel through protrusions called cytonemes directly from the source cells to the target cells (Akiyama and Gibson, 2015; Bressloff and Kim, 2018; Kornberg and Roy, 2014; Müller et al., 2013; Wilcockson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a description of the DT model supported by multiple citations.

claim: The concentration of morphogen as a function of distance from the source cells has been observed to follow an exponential distribution for a variety of different morphogens.
source: The concentration of morphogen as a function of distance from the source cells has been observed to follow an exponential distribution for a variety of different morphogens (Driever and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1988; Houchmandzadeh et al., 2002).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by citations.

claim: The accumulation times for several morphogens in Drosophila have been measured and found to match the predictions made by the SDC model.
source: The accumulation times for several morphogens in Drosophila have been measured and found to match the predictions made by the SDC model (Berezhkovskii et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by citation.

claim: In zebrafish, the molecular dynamics of the morphogen Fgf8 have been measured and found to be consistent with Brownian diffusion through extracellular space.
source: In zebrafish, the molecular dynamics of the morphogen Fgf8 have been measured and found to be consistent with Brownian diffusion through extracellular space (Yu et al., 2009).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by citation.

claim: The establishment of the Hedgehog morphogen gradient in Drosophila is highly correlated in both space and time with the formation of cytonemes.
source: The establishment of the Hedgehog morphogen gradient in Drosophila is highly correlated in both space and time with the formation of cytonemes (Bischoff et al., 2013)
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by citation.

claim: Wnt morphogens have been found to be highly localized around cell protrusions such as cytonemes.
source: while Wnt morphogens have been found to be highly localized around cell protrusions such as cytonemes (Huang and Kornberg, 2015; Stanganello and Scholpp, 2016).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by citations.

claim: It remains unknown whether one model allows for a cell to sense its local morphogen concentration more precisely than the other given biological parameters such as the number of cells or the characteristic lengthscale of the profile.
source: In particular, it remains unknown whether one model allows for a cell to sense its local morphogen concentration more precisely than the other given biological parameters such as the number of cells or the characteristic lengthscale of the profile.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge that the manuscript addresses.

claim: Most experimental measurements used for comparison were taken during stages when the steady state approximation is valid.
source: Here, we model profiles in the steady state regime, as most of the experimental measurements to which we will later compare our results were taken during stages when the steady state approximation is valid (Grimm et al., 2010; Gregor et al., 2007b; Kicheva et al., 2007; Yu et al., 2009; Kanodia et al., 2009).
evidence: This justifies the steady-state assumption and is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Precision depends not only on stochastic fluctuations in the morphogen concentration, but also on the shape of the mean morphogen profile.
source: Precision depends not only on stochastic fluctuations in the morphogen concentration, but also on the shape of the mean morphogen profile, as the shape determines concentration differences between adjacent cells that may adopt different fates.
evidence: This is a theoretical consideration based on the definition of precision used in the study.

claim: Cytonemes are tubular protrusions that are hundreds of nanometers thick and between several and hundreds of microns long.
source: Cytonemes are tubular protrusions that are hundreds of nanometers thick and between several and hundreds of microns long (Kornberg and Roy, 2014; Kornberg, 2014).
evidence: This is a description of cytoneme structure supported by citations.

claim: Cytonemes are supported by actin filaments, and morphogen molecules are thought to be actively transported along the filaments via molecular motors.
source: They are supported by actin filaments, and it is thought that morphogen molecules are actively transported along the filaments via molecular motors (Kornberg and Roy, 2014; Kornberg, 2014; Sanders et al., 2013; Huang and Kornberg, 2015).
evidence: This is a description of cytoneme function supported by citations, with speculative language ('it is thought').

claim: A DT model that includes forward and backward transport of molecules within cytonemes reproduces experimentally measured accumulation times.
source: It was recently shown that a DT model that includes forward and backward transport of molecules within cytonemes reproduces experimentally measured accumulation times (Teimouri and Kolomeisky, 2016a; Bressloff and Kim, 2018)
evidence: This is a finding from previous theoretical work supported by citations.

claim: The noise properties of the DT model with forward and backward transport were not previously considered.
source: It was recently shown that a DT model that includes forward and backward transport of molecules within cytonemes reproduces experimentally measured accumulation times (Teimouri and Kolomeisky, 2016a; Bressloff and Kim, 2018), although the noise properties of this model were not considered.
evidence: This identifies a gap in previous work that the current manuscript addresses.

claim: Any system in which molecules can only degrade in the target cells and cannot leave the target cells has the steady-state statistical properties of a simple birth-death process.
source: In fact, here we prove that any system in which molecules can only degrade in the target cells and cannot leave the target cells has the steady-state statistical properties of a simple birth-death process.
evidence: This is a theoretical result proven in the manuscript through mathematical derivation.

claim: The transport process in the DT model adds no noise to mj.
source: Despite the complexity of the transport process in Equation 1, we find that it adds no noise to mj.
evidence: This is a theoretical finding derived from the mathematical analysis in the manuscript.

claim: The optimum precision in the DT model occurs at an intermediate value of ϕ between exponential and power-law profiles.
source: the optimum is in between.
evidence: This is inferred from the trade-off between amplitude and steepness.

claim: In the SDC model, morphogen molecules can diffuse both into and out of the target cells.
source: Importantly, in the model presented here the morphogen molecules can diffuse both into and out of the target cells, thus violating the condition that they can only degrade once in a target cell and disallowing our previous argument depicted in Figure 2.
evidence: This is a key distinction between the SDC and DT models stated explicitly.

claim: In the SDC model, molecules can leave a target cell not only by degradation, but also by diffusion.
source: It reflects the fact that, unlike in the DT model, molecules can leave a target cell not only by degradation, but also by diffusion.
evidence: This is a key mechanistic difference between the models.

claim: The crossover between DT and SDC precision holds for 1D, 2D, and 3D geometries.
source: This effect holds for a single source cell providing morphogen for a 1D line of target cells as well as for a 1D line of source cells with a 2D sheet of target cells and a 2D sheet of source cells with a 3D volume of target cells.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B and discussed in the text.

claim: The DT model is more precise for short profiles because it has a larger amplitude.
source: Conversely, the reason that the DT model is more precise for short profiles is that it has a larger amplitude.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the amplitude scaling of the two models.

claim: The morphogen Wingless (Wg) is localized near cell protrusions such as cytonemes.
source: In Drosophila, the morphogen Wingless (Wg) is localized near cell protrusions such as cytonemes (Huang and Kornberg, 2015; Stanganello and Scholpp, 2016)
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by citations.

claim: The Hedgehog (Hh) gradient correlates highly in both space and time with the formation of cytonemes.
source: and the Hedgehog (Hh) gradient correlates highly in both space and time with the formation of cytonemes (Bischoff et al., 2013)
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by citation.

claim: Wg and Hh morphogen profiles are suggested to be formed via a DT mechanism.
source: suggesting that these two morphogen profiles are formed via a DT mechanism.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations of cytoneme involvement.

claim: Bicoid has been understood as a model example of SDC for decades.
source: Conversely, Bicoid has been understood as a model example of SDC for decades (Driever and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1988; Gregor et al., 2007a; Houchmandzadeh et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Dorsal is spread by diffusion, but its absorption is localized to a specific region of target cells via a nonuniform degradation mechanism.
source: Similarly, Dorsal is spread by diffusion; however, its absorption is localized to a specific region of target cells via a nonuniform degradation mechanism, making it more complex than the simple SDC model (Carrell et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by citation.

claim: For Dpp there is evidence for a variety of different gradient formation mechanisms.
source: Finally, for Dpp there is evidence for a variety of different gradient formation mechanisms (Akiyama and Gibson, 2015; Müller et al., 2013; Wilcockson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: The morphogen Fgf8 in zebrafish has been studied at the single molecule level and found to have molecular dynamics closely matching the Brownian movement expected in an SDC mechanism.
source: In zebrafish, the morphogen Fgf8 has been studied at the single molecule level and found to have molecular dynamics closely matching the Brownian movement expected in an SDC mechanism (Yu et al., 2009).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by citation.

claim: Cyclops, Squint, Lefty1, and Lefty2 have been shown to spread diffusively and affect cells distant from their source.
source: Similarly, Cyclops, Squint, Lefty1, and Lefty2, all of which are involved in the Nodal/Lefty system, have been shown to spread diffusively and affect cells distant from their source (Müller et al., 2013; Rogers and Müller, 2019).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by citations.

claim: Cyclops and Squint have been argued to be tightly regulated via a Gierer-Meinhardt type system, diminishing their gradient sizes to values much lower than what they would be without this regulation.
source: This would support the SDC mechanism, although Cyclops and Squint have been argued to be tightly regulated via a Gierer-Meinhardt type system, thus diminishing their gradient sizes to values much lower than what they would be without this regulation (Gierer and Meinhardt, 1972; Rogers and Müller, 2019).
evidence: This is a theoretical interpretation supported by citations.

claim: Morphogens with evidence for DT, SDC, or multiple mechanisms correspond to short, long, and intermediate profile lengths, respectively.
source: We see that in general, the three cases correspond to short, long, and intermediate profile lengths, respectively, which is qualitatively consistent with our predictions.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A by comparing experimental data with mechanism type.

claim: The theory predicts the correct threshold: morphogens with evidence for either DT or SDC fall into the regime in which that mechanism is predicted to be more precise for most cells.
source: We see that our theory predicts the correct threshold: the morphogens for which the evidence suggests either a DT or an SDC mechanism (red or blue) fall into the regime in which we predict that mechanism to be more precise for most of the cells
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4B by comparing theoretical predictions with experimental data.

claim: Morphogens with multiple mechanisms fall in between the DT and SDC regimes.
source: and the morphogens with multiple mechanisms (white) fall in between.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The quantitative agreement between theory and data provides support for the idea that morphogen profiles form according to the mechanism that maximizes the sensory precision of the target cells.
source: This result provides quantitative support for the idea that morphogen profiles form according to the mechanism that maximizes the sensory precision of the target cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the agreement between theoretical predictions and experimental observations shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The DT model benefits from larger molecule numbers and no added noise from the transport process.
source: While the DT model benefits from larger molecule numbers and no added noise from the transport process
evidence: This is derived from the theoretical analysis of the DT model.

claim: The ability of molecules to diffuse into and away from a target cell in the SDC model allows the cell to measure a greater number of effectively unique molecules in the same time frame.
source: the ability of molecules to diffuse into and away from a target cell in the SDC model allows the cell to measure a greater number of effectively unique molecules in the same time frame.
evidence: This is derived from the theoretical analysis of the SDC model, specifically the correlation time.

claim: Morphogen profiles with shorter lengths should utilize cytonemes or some other form of direct transport mechanism.
source: we predicted that morphogen profiles with shorter lengths should utilize cytonemes or some other form of direct transport mechanism
evidence: This is a prediction derived from the theoretical analysis.

claim: Morphogens with longer profiles should rely on extracellular diffusion.
source: whereas morphogens with longer profiles should rely on extracellular diffusion
evidence: This is a prediction derived from the theoretical analysis.

claim: The prediction that mechanism choice depends on profile length is in quantitative agreement with measurements on known morphogens.
source: a prediction that is in quantitative agreement with measurements on known morphogens.
evidence: This is supported by the comparison shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The models presented are minimal and cannot be directly applied to all systems.
source: Despite the quantitative agreement between our theory and experiments, it is clear that the models presented here are minimal and thus cannot be directly applied to all systems.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of the limitations of the theoretical models.

claim: The SDC model can be violated if the diffusion of morphogen through a biological environment is hindered by crowding, leading to possibly subdiffusive behavior.
source: Additionally, the SDC model can be violated if the diffusion of morphogen through a biological environment is hindered by the typically crowded nature of such environments, leading to possibly subdiffusive behavior (Ellery et al., 2014; Fanelli and McKane, 2010).
evidence: This is a theoretical consideration supported by citations.

claim: The dynamics of the cytonemes themselves were explicitly ignored because the growth rate of cytonemes is sufficiently fast to traverse the entire system size in significantly less time than is required for cells to integrate their morphogen counts.
source: For the DT model, we explicitly ignored the dynamics of the cytonemes themselves due to the growth rate of the cytonemes being sufficiently fast so as to traverse the entire system size in significantly less time than is required for the cells to integrate their morphogen counts over (Bischoff et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a modeling assumption justified by citations to experimental observations.

claim: The assumption of fast cytoneme growth is problematic if cytonemes continue to behave dynamically after reaching the source cell.
source: This assumption is problematic if cytonemes continue to behave dynamically after reaching the source cell.
evidence: This is a discussion of limitations of the modeling assumptions.

claim: The process of cytonemes switching between phases of growing and retracting can introduce super-Poissonian noise sources to the morphogen count within the target cells.
source: In particular, the process of cytonemes switching between phases of growing and retracting can introduce super-Poissonian noise sources to the morphogen count within the target cells.
evidence: This is a theoretical consideration about potential noise sources not included in the model.

claim: Super-Poissonian noise can be introduced by relaxing the assumption that morphogen molecules behave independently of each other.
source: Super-Poissonian noise can also be introduced by relaxing the assumption that the morphogen molecules behave independently of each other as this was a critical component of our proof that the molecule count in the target cells is statistically identical to a birth-death process.
evidence: This is a theoretical consideration about the consequences of relaxing model assumptions.

claim: A hybrid system which utilizes a combination of diffusion and directed transport is conceivable.
source: Finally, it is conceivable that a hybrid system which utilizes a combination of diffusion and directed transport could be developed.
evidence: This is speculation about possible extensions of the work.

claim: The authors are unaware of any experimental study into a hybrid diffusion-direct transport system.
source: However, we are unaware of any experimental study into such a possibility and as such have not considered it in this particular work.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of experimental knowledge.
